qAndA.answer: The direction of the angular displacement vector is along the axis of rotation.

qAndA.answer: Angular position and angular displacement are considered vectors because they are displacements from a defined origin.
qAndA.question: Why are angular position and angular displacement considered vectors?

narrativeProgression.description: The professor introduces the concept of angular displacement in rotational motion.
He emphasizes that angular displacement depends on both the object (its shape and orientation) and the axis of rotation.
The professor uses a teflon rod as a visual aid to illustrate angular displacement.
He defines an axis of rotation along the back of the rod, and demonstrates how the rod rotates around this axis.
The professor draws diagrams on the whiteboard to illustrate different angular positions and displacements of the rod.
He introduces the concept of the origin in angular displacement, and defines theta = 0 as the flat position of the rod.
The professor explains that the angular displacement is the change in angular position, and calculates the angular displacement for different rotations of the rod.
He points out that angular displacement is a vector, just like translational displacement.
The professor mentions that the direction of the angular displacement vector is along the axis of rotation.
He further explains that both angular position and angular displacement are vectors because they are displacements from the origin.
